answer: Agents bidding to inspect a terrace or jetty receive work through a lottery weighted by locked collateral, with no bonus per account. A public random beacon selects among escrowed units, and a unit cannot back overlapping bids. Splitting 100 units among 100 aliases leaves the same total selection probability, so clones cannot forge extra lottery weight. Buying more influence requires more capital held until inspection ends. This makes identity splitting neutral, not wealth harmless; independent audits must still check the work.
